prompt: My side project gradient-svg-generator (repo at D:\github_repository\gradient-svg-generator, live at gradient-svg-generator.vercel.app) serves 340+ animated gradient SVG banner templates for GitHub READMEs — you embed a single URL, no install; there's also a visual editor and template gallery. It's free, MIT, and other people's READMEs already embed it, which means MY Vercel account pays for THEIR traffic. I want to (a) know the real competitive landscape — things like capsule-render and readme-typing-svg exist, (b) get positioning copy that won't fall apart under scrutiny — can I honestly claim to be 'the largest animated README banner collection' or is that going to blow up in my face, and (c) an honest read on whether/how to monetize this or whether I should just cap the costs and keep it as a portfolio piece.

assertions.name: largest-claim-explicitly-audited
assertions.text: The 'largest animated README banner collection' superlative is explicitly audited against named competitors (e.g. template/feature counts of capsule-render and others) BEFORE being endorsed or rejected, with a clear verdict.

assertions.name: defensible-narrower-claim-supplied
assertions.text: A narrower, defensible positioning claim is supplied (whether or not the superlative survives), phrased so a hostile commenter cannot refute it in one search.

assertions.name: competitor-table-with-sources
assertions.text: At least 5 named competitors/alternatives in the README-widget ecosystem appear with source URLs.

assertions.name: hostile-scrutiny-pass-present
assertions.text: A red-team/objections/banned-claims artifact exists that anticipates hostile comments (the user explicitly fears a repeat of being 'destroyed in the comments').

assertions.name: monetization-verdict-addresses-freerider-costs
assertions.text: An explicit monetization-vs-portfolio verdict is given that concretely addresses the free-rider embed-traffic cost problem (caps, sponsorship, paid tiers, or a reasoned 'keep it free'), not generic monetization advice.

assertions.name: falsification-section-present
assertions.text: The deliverable includes an explicit falsification section (e.g. 'What would prove this wrong').
